Dive Buddy
Alert Band

Buddy communication starts with attention.

Underwater, even a simple message starts with getting the other diver to look. Dive Buddy Alert Band is Rafael’s concept for that first moment: a button calls the paired band, a vibration requests attention, and a display shows the response and available distance.

A concept by Rafael. An aid to buddy procedures, never a safety guarantee.

Discover the ideaTry the buddy call

Something to share.
A buddy looking elsewhere.

A formation in the reef. A change of plan. A routine check-in. The message may be simple, but a hand signal only starts working when the other diver sees it. DBA focuses on the step before that exchange: a direct request for one buddy’s attention.

A call that belongs to your buddy.

The idea is a paired connection. Before the dive, two bands are linked. During the dive, a deliberate press requests a tactile alert on the other band. The receiving diver presses to acknowledge, so the caller can distinguish a device reply from a person’s response.

Feel the request. Understand the response.

The vibration is intended to interrupt attention briefly; the screen explains why. It shows an incoming call, a buddy’s acknowledgement, and fresh separation estimates during a ranging session. If a current reading is unavailable, the number clears rather than lingering as if it were still valid.

This is a communication aid for divers who already use buddy procedures. It does not establish bearing, provide a route, or guarantee reunion.

A request. A response.
A clearer picture.

Follow the proposed exchange between two divers. Call the paired band, have the other diver acknowledge, then request distance feedback. The screens distinguish each step so a device reply cannot be mistaken for a person’s response.

Interactive demonstration with simulated readings. The physical top button controls the proposed interaction; underwater performance remains unverified.

Each control represents the same physical top button. Select a labeled hold action to simulate that gesture.

Move the slider while ranging. Fresh simulated readings arrive once a second. Beyond the 20 m target, this demo shows an unavailable link.

Visible pulses are always available. Optional phone vibration illustrates one band at a time; browser support varies.

Explore connection and battery states

Battery values are fixed demo examples, not measured charge or runtime. Low battery permits a call but pauses distance feedback in this proposed interface. A 3 s stale-reading cutoff is illustrative.

Call confirmation.

A device receiving a message is different from a diver responding. The buddy explicitly acknowledges the call before the caller starts distance feedback.

Distance and direction.

A distance reading shows separation. It does not show where to swim, which way either diver is facing, or whether a route is clear. The one-transducer concept does not provide bearing.

Button behavior and feedback
Pair on the surface

Hold both buttons for 3 seconds. Both displays show the paired state.

Call and acknowledge

Short press to call. The receiving band gives three attention pulses; its diver short presses to acknowledge. A short press on the caller cancels.

Read the distance

After acknowledgement, the caller holds for 1 second. Both divers see separation; the buddy also sees that the session is active. Either diver short presses to stop.

When a reading disappears

A missing or stale reply clears the distance and its trend, and suppresses distance pulses. The display resumes only after a fresh simulated reply.

Optional cadence: at least 15 m, one pulse every 4 s; 10–15 m, every 2 s; 5–10 m, every second; 2–5 m, a double pulse every 0.5 s. Below 2 m, a 1 s burst ends the session. Sessions also end after 5 minutes. These inherited concept behaviors do not confirm visual contact or reunion.

Trend compares successive simulated distances; it is not a direction arrow. Numbers, link behavior, acknowledgement policy, stale timing and display layout are interface proposals. Acoustic accuracy, real-world readability, power and enclosure integration remain unestablished. DBA is an aid to buddy procedures, never a safety guarantee.

Made to slip on.

The band is intended to be flexible silicone: it stretches over the hand, then sits around the wrist or suit cuff. The sealed electronics remain in a rigid, removable module. The circular CAD view shows the band at rest; it does not represent a rigid bracelet.

One reference size. A fit range to define.

The current model represents one reference size, with a 62 mm relaxed opening and approximately 195 mm inner circumference. A finished size range needs to account for wrist and suit-cuff circumference, hand passage, comfort and module retention. No wrist-size coverage or safe extension has been established.

Silicone grade, hardness, force to stretch, recovery and maximum extension remain undefined. The flex view illustrates intended behavior; it is not a material simulation.

A closer look at the design.

The flexible band carries a rigid, sealed module that can be removed when the band needs replacing. Inside, the display and its window sit beside the physical top button. Explore the 14-part assembly in its relaxed shape below.

Sealed charging

The receiver coil sits beneath the button side of the sealed cap, separate from the display envelope. It is intended to receive power without an exposed charging connector.

The trade-off is a dedicated dock, alignment and thermal design, plus an approximately two-hour charge target. Inductive charging alone does not establish waterproofing or eliminate all sealing risks.

A module that stays with you

The module is intended to release from the silicone cradle so the band can be replaced. The cap remains sealed. Retention, service method and battery replacement policy still need definition.

Dimensions behind the form.

The nominal housing is 44 × 32 × 17.5 mm, with a separate 2.2 mm button protrusion. These views show how the display, controls and internal component envelopes relate to that space.

CAD Rev D · The band is shown at rest. Overall height, including the button, is 90.7 mm. Display active area is 14 × 16 mm. These are concept dimensions; manufacturing tolerances and pressure performance remain undefined.

From product intent to engineering detail.

A useful buddy call depends on more than the enclosure. Acoustic reception, message acknowledgement, legible feedback and comfortable retention have to work together. The specification records what the concept defines and what each discipline still needs to resolve.

The proposed link uses approximately 65 kHz ultrasonic two-way timing to estimate separation, with a 20 m range target. One transducer provides distance; it does not locate the buddy’s bearing or measure relative orientation.

Interface & interaction7 items
AreaIntent and statusEngineering notes / discipline
PairingProposed behavior

Hold both buttons 3 s on the surface; show the paired buddy and Ready on both displays. The 16-bit pair code remains a Rev A protocol assumption.

Engineering notesAddress allocation, cross-pair isolation and re-pairing protocol remain open. The simulation stages mutual pairing; it does not discover real devices.Firmware
Call and acknowledgementProposed behavior

Short press calls the paired buddy. B receives three alert pulses and an incoming-call screen; B short presses to acknowledge. A distinguishes Calling, Device received and Buddy acknowledged.

Engineering notesTransport acknowledgement confirms the device received a packet, not human attention. Retry limits, collision handling and delayed or duplicated messages need protocol definition.Firmware / interaction design
Ranging and stopProposed behavior

Caller holds 1 s to request ranging after explicit buddy acknowledgement. Both displays show fresh distance when available; caller cadence is optional. During ranging, a short press on either band stops; nominal 5-minute timeout.

Engineering notesRemote stop requires confirmation. The demonstration separates local stop from unconfirmed delivery when the link is unavailable. Both displays and synchronization remain proposed firmware behavior.Firmware / interaction design
Haptic vocabularyProposed behavior

Attention uses three pulses. Optional caller distance cadence retains Rev A: 15-20 m pulse/4 s; 10-15 m pulse/2 s; 5-10 m pulse/s; 2-5 m double pulse/0.5 s; below 2 m a 1 s burst then stop.

Engineering notesDisplay provides distance without requiring cadence interpretation. Actual intensity, perceptibility through cuffs, hysteresis and waveforms remain unresolved. Near does not mean visual contact or reunion.Interaction design / firmware
Lost linkProposed behavior

Missing or stale replies clear the current distance and trend and suppress proximity pulses. Display reads Distance unavailable; a fresh valid update is required to restore a number.

Engineering notesDemonstration freshness timeout and quality switches are illustrative. Production age limits, validation, outlier handling and reacquisition require acoustic and firmware definition.Systems / firmware
Display and readabilityRev D display proposal

Display body 16 × 18 × 2.5 mm; window 18 × 20 × 1.2 mm; active area 14 × 16 mm. Proposed screens show buddy, call state, fresh distance, unavailable data and battery.

Engineering notesThese are concept envelopes, not selected display specifications. Whole-metre synthetic demo values do not establish accuracy. Display technology, pixel layout, brightness, viewing angle and underwater legibility require definition.Interaction design / electronics / mechanical
Distance trendProposed behavior

Nearer / farther is an optional textual comparison of successive fresh distance estimates. It describes separation change, not a route or direction to swim.

Engineering notesThe simulator uses controlled values. Sampling interval, deadband, stability, quality gating and outlier rejection need definition before a measured trend can be shown.Firmware / interaction design
Acoustics & direction4 items
AreaIntent and statusEngineering notes / discipline
Acoustic methodFixed decision

Approximately 65 kHz ultrasonic two-way time-of-flight; one wrist transducer.

Engineering notesTransducer construction/resonance, directivity, drive level, link budget and receiver sensitivity need engineering definition. Component names in Rev A are candidates, not selections.Underwater acoustics
Distance and timingProposed target

20 m range; approximately ±0.3 m distance target; nominal 1 Hz exchange with assumed fixed 2 ms reply delay.

Engineering notesNo measured performance supplied. Accuracy, resolution, latency and availability need separate definitions. Use d = (RTT - reply delay) × sound speed / 2; timing precision alone does not establish accuracy.Acoustics / firmware
Orientation and echoesOpen question

Body shadowing, wrist orientation, obstructions, other pairs and multipath may affect reception or range.

Engineering notesDefine accepted environments, range-quality reporting, outlier handling and stale-reading policy. No directional arrow is provided to the diver.Underwater acoustics
Direction and orientationOutside current capability

One-transducer two-way timing provides range. No buddy bearing, relative heading or depth difference is measured or displayed.

Engineering notesA directional buddy-finding feature requires separately defined sensing and estimation. Exchanging device headings alone does not determine relative location; wrist heading is not necessarily swimming direction.Systems / underwater acoustics

Engineering review notes
  • Display integration: the window, display body, coil and button plunger have defined envelopes in the concept model. Window attachment, optical performance, wiring, supports and charging efficiency remain engineering decisions.
  • Internal clearance: the receiver coil now sits under the button side of the cap, beside the display. Solid-envelope checks do not establish routing, assembly method, moving clearances or thermal performance.
  • Band fit: the 62 mm relaxed opening is one reference size. Silicone grade, hardness, extension, hand passage and wrist/cuff coverage remain undefined.
  • Power: the display requires a revised energy budget. Historical current and capacity assumptions do not establish runtime for this version.
  • Drawing authority: current dimensions are drawn from the Rev D source and regenerated geometry. No manufacturing tolerances have been released.

Designed around the pair.

A buddy call is useful only when both divers can participate. The proposed product is therefore a pair of bands with one shared inductive charging dock. Recreational buddy pairs are the initial audience; instructors and dive shops are potential places to introduce the concept.

The commercial question is whether an addressed tactile call and readable separation information are valuable enough to earn space on both divers’ wrists. The current package defines that proposition; customer demand and the display variant’s cost remain unestablished.

The current work brings together the interaction, the parametric assembly and the engineering brief. Underwater performance, manufacturability and delivered economics remain to be established.

Original cost basis

The display-free Rev A concept used a $179–199 retail target per pair and an estimated $86 per pair at 5,000 pairs, ±30%, including dock allocation. These are historical desk estimates, excluding tooling, engineering, freight and duty. The current display variant has no revised cost estimate or retail target.
